verdict: Cross-observable check: parameters fit to H(theta) predict the area and edge observables better under Helfrich (linear) (total log-RMSE 0.066 vs 0.108). On the pseudo-temporally-SORTED static population, the non-cooperative linear relaxation generalizes across observables better than CoopCM -- the opposite of the paper's DYNAMIC per-cell fit, and expected: sorting by theta discards the real timing the cooperative law was fit to. This is a geometry result, not a force result; force stays refused.

provenance.paper: Mund, Tschanz, ... Ries, J Cell Biol 2023
provenance.method: fit H(theta), map params onto A(theta) & E(theta) (Mund et al. 2023 Fig. 3 B-D method)
provenance.caveat: A and E are deterministic functions of (1/H, theta) on a theta-sorted population; they reweight theta-domain leverage, they do not add an independent measurement axis
